primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Surfactant protein B deficiency due to SFTPB loss of function
mechanism: Surfactant protein B is essential for normal pulmonary surfactant organization and function, including intracellular packaging of surfactant components and formation/presentation of the phospholipid film at the alveolar air-liquid interface. Biallelic SFTPB loss can cause severe refractory neonatal respiratory failure even in term infants.
vignette: A full-term newborn develops severe hypoxemic respiratory failure within hours of birth. Chest imaging shows diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities. Cultures are negative, echocardiography shows no structural heart disease, and repeated exogenous surfactant administration produces only transient improvement. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SFTPB.
lead: Which of the following best explains the primary pulmonary defect in this infant?
correct: Failure of normal surfactant organization and formation of a stable phospholipid film at the alveolar air-liquid interface
distractors: Failure of chloride secretion from airway epithelial cells
Defective ciliary dynein causing impaired mucociliary clearance
Loss of alpha-1 antitrypsin protection against neutrophil elastase
Failure of pulmonary vascular smooth muscle to respond to nitric oxide
distractor_notes: CFTR-mediated chloride transport causes cystic fibrosis and does not explain immediate severe term-neonatal respiratory failure from SFTPB variants.
Primary ciliary dyskinesia causes impaired mucociliary clearance, neonatal respiratory symptoms, and later sinopulmonary disease but is not a surfactant-protein defect.
Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency predisposes to emphysema and liver disease rather than congenital surfactant failure.
Pulmonary vascular nitric-oxide signaling pertains to vascular tone; SFTPB loss directly disrupts alveolar surfactant function.
key_expl: SP-B is crucial for pulmonary surfactant metabolism and physical function, including packaging of surfactant components and formation/presentation of the phospholipid monolayer at the alveolar air-liquid interface. Complete SFTPB deficiency causes severe, often lethal respiratory failure in term infants.
objective: Explain severe neonatal respiratory failure in SFTPB deficiency as failure of normal pulmonary surfactant organization and alveolar phospholipid-film function.
